mainTopic: Why women are exempt from קרחה (אביי and רבא on איסי), the meaning of ״בנים אתם״, and the new משנה on Temple services done only by men.
overview: The amud opens with the last words of an earlier statement. אביי then explains why איסי exempts women from the ban on making a bald spot (קרחה) in mourning. איסי learns it through a גזירה שוה from the כהנים, where the תורה speaks only to the sons of Aaron. The גמרא challenges this: the same גזירה שוה is already used in a ברייתא for other laws about bald spots. It answers that the longer word קרחה, where קרח would have been enough, lets us learn two things. רבא gives a different source, from ״בין עיניכם״ by תפילין, and the גמרא explains why each אמורא does not accept the other's reason. The גמרא then asks what ״בנים אתם״ teaches, and brings the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר over whether Israel is always called God's children. Finally, a new משנה lists Temple service actions done by men and not women. The גמרא begins giving a פסוק for each one, and the source for receiving the blood continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing words of the earlier statement
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the earlier discussion: 'it is one.'
steps.simpleTranslation: ...are one.
steps.whatsHappening: These two words finish a statement that began before this section. They wrap up the earlier point before אביי starts something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא is saying that the cases it was just comparing count as one single prohibition, not two separate ones. This closes the earlier topic and clears the way for אביי's explanation of איסי.

keyTerms.meaning: It is one (one and the same prohibition)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to read this as a full sentence by itself. It is the tail end of a statement from before this section.

phrases.english: are one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the statement left open from before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The cases under discussion count as one single prohibition.

steps.title: אביי explains איסי's source: a גזירה שוה from the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: אביי says איסי learns 'קרחה' (baldness) said to all Jews from 'קרחה' said to the כהנים. Women are exempt there, so they are exempt here too.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is איסי's reason. He learns 'baldness' from 'baldness' said about the sons of Aaron. Just as there women are exempt, so too here women are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why איסי holds that women are not included in the prohibition of making a bald spot in grief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'קרחה' appears in the פסוק for all Jews and also in the פסוק for כהנים. The כהנים פסוק is addressed to 'בני אהרן' (sons, not daughters), so there women are exempt. The matching word links the two places, so the exemption for women carries over to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who explains איסי's view here
A תנא who exempts women from the prohibition of קרחה
Making a bald spot, as a sign of mourning
He learns (one law from another)
The sons of Aaron, the כהנים

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic גזירה שוה: one shared word carries a detail (here, that women are exempt) from one law over to another.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.notes: The word appears in דברים 14:1 for all Jews and in ויקרא 21:5 for the כהנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new point: the source behind איסי's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: איסי exempts women from קרחה through a גזירה שוה from the כהנים, where only sons are commanded.

steps.title: A קל וחומר would be enough, so why write the פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: If 'sons of Aaron' covers the whole chapter, then a קל וחומר from the כהנים would already exempt women among ordinary Jews. So why does the תורה need to write the קרחה prohibition for all Jews in a way that sets up the גזירה שוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if we hold that when the verse is written, it is written for the whole topic, let the verse be silent about it, and it could come through a קל וחומר. I would say: If כהנים, for whom the verse added extra מצוות, are commanded as 'sons of Aaron' and not daughters of Aaron, then ordinary Jews, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's explanation. It says we don't need this verse and its גזירה שוה, because simple logic would already give us the same result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Assume the words 'בני אהרן' at the start of the chapter apply to every law in it, including קרחה. Then כהנים, who have more מצוות, still exclude their women. Ordinary Jews, who have fewer מצוות, should certainly exclude women too. So the extra verse looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: For the whole topic (the whole chapter)
Let the verse be silent about it (it need not be written)
A 'how much more so' argument, from a stricter case to a lighter one
Extra מצוות
Is it not all the more so?

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'בני אהרן' covers the whole chapter, a קל וחומר from כהנים (more מצוות, yet women exempt) already exempts women among ordinary Jews.

steps.title: Without the גזירה שוה, we'd think the topic broke off
steps.stepSummary: The גזירה שוה is needed. Without it, we would say the topic stopped after the laws of טומאה, so 'sons of Aaron' would not reach the קרחה law.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not for the גזירה שוה, I would have said: the topic was interrupted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and shows why the גזירה שוה is really needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר only works if 'בני אהרן' covers the קרחה law. But the laws of טומאה might have ended that topic. If so, the קרחה rule for כהנים would include their daughters, and nothing could be learned for women. The גזירה שוה shows that women are exempt from קרחה anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: If not for
A link between two laws through a matching word
I would have thought
The topic was interrupted (it broke off)

steps.whatToRemember: איסי exempts women from קרחה through the גזירה שוה 'קרחה'-'קרחה' with the כהנים. A קל וחומר cannot replace it, since we might have thought the topic of 'sons of Aaron' broke off before the קרחה law.

phrases.english: If not for the gezeira shava
I would have said: the topic was interrupted.
phrases.notes: He means the laws of טומאה might end the 'sons of Aaron' topic, so the קרחה rule for כהנים would include daughters too.

steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה is needed to show that women are exempt from קרחה.

steps.title: Even now, maybe the topic stopped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the argument of step 4 back around. Even with the גזירה שוה, why not say the 'sons of Aaron' topic stopped after the laws of טומאה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now too, let us say the topic stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 4. It asks why we shouldn't still say that the section about 'sons of Aaron' ended after the laws of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the topic stopped. Then the קרחה rule for כהנים would apply to daughters of כהנים too, since only the טומאה laws were limited to males. If so, the כהנים rule does not show that women are exempt, so there is no exemption to carry over to ordinary Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: Now too, meaning even according to the answer just given
Let us say
The topic stopped, so a phrase at the start of a section no longer reaches the later laws

phrases.english: Now too, let us say the topic stopped,

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the כהנים law exempts women, so the exemption can be carried over to all Jews
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the topic stopped, the כהנים קרחה law includes women, so there is no exemption to learn from.

steps.title: The גזירה שוה is already used for something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks an expected reply. If you answer that the גזירה שוה itself teaches the women's exemption, that גזירה שוה is already needed for a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is because of the גזירה שוה, that is needed for what a ברייתא teaches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expects someone to answer, 'We know women are exempt because of the גזירה שוה.' It replies that the גזירה שוה is already busy teaching other laws, and it is setting up a ברייתא to prove this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה is normally used for one lesson. If the words 'קרחה' and 'קרחה' are already used to share other details between כהנים and ordinary Jews, they seem unavailable to teach the women's exemption. The next steps quote the ברייתא that shows those other uses.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching drawn from the same word appearing in two places in the תורה
It is needed for, meaning it is already used for another lesson

steps.title: Each bald spot counts separately
steps.stepSummary: First part of the ברייתא. The word קרחה teaches that a person is liable for every single bald spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They shall not make bald.' You might think that even if he made four or five bald spots, he is liable only once. So the verse says 'baldness,' to make him liable for each one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the ברייתא. Its first lesson is that every bald spot is a separate sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verb 'לא יקרחו' alone might mean only one punishment, however many spots there are. The added word 'קרחה' (a bald spot) makes each spot its own sin. This is the first job the word קרחה already has.

So the verse teaches
Bald spots
Each and every one

steps.title: The whole head counts, not just between the eyes
steps.stepSummary: Second part of the ברייתא. The word 'בראשם' teaches that a כהן is liable for a bald spot anywhere on the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the verse say 'on their head'? Since it says 'do not make a bald spot between your eyes for the dead,' you might think he is liable only between the eyes. How do we include the whole head? The verse says 'on their head,' to make him liable on the whole head just as between the eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second lesson. For כהנים, a bald spot anywhere on the head is forbidden, not only the spot between the eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse for all Jews mentions only 'between your eyes.' The word 'בראשם' in the כהנים verse widens the rule to the whole head, at least for כהנים. The next step will carry this over to ordinary Jews.

To include

steps.title: The גזירה שוה carries both rules to all Jews
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא uses the גזירה שוה of 'קרחה' and 'קרחה' to apply both rules to ordinary Jews: each spot counts, and the whole head counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know this about כהנים, since the תורה gave them extra מצוות. How do we know it for ordinary Jews? 'Baldness' is said here and 'baldness' is said there. Just as here he is liable for each bald spot and for the whole head like between the eyes, so too there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now uses the very same גזירה שוה to carry the two rules from כהנים over to all Jews. This shows the גזירה שוה is being used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot just assume ordinary Jews share these rules, because כהנים have extra מצוות. The matching word 'קרחה' in both verses links them. That puts the גזירה שוה to work, which is exactly the challenge from step 6.

steps.title: כהנים are forbidden only over a dead person
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by using the גזירה שוה in the other direction. Like ordinary Jews, כהנים are forbidden to make a bald spot only as mourning for the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as there it is about a dead person, so too here it is about a dead person.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with one more lesson from the same גזירה שוה. This time a detail moves from the verse for all Jews over to the כהנים verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse for all Jews says 'for the dead.' Through the גזירה שוה, the כהנים prohibition is also limited to mourning the dead. So the גזירה שוה is working hard in both directions, which seems to leave no room to teach the women's exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: Over a dead person, meaning as a sign of mourning

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא uses the קרחה גזירה שוה for several laws: each spot counts, the whole head counts, ordinary Jews are included, and כהנים are forbidden only over the dead.

steps.title: The longer word teaches two things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תורה could have written the short word 'קרח' but wrote 'קרחה.' This extra form lets us learn two lessons.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse write 'bald.' Why does it say 'baldness'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of steps 5 and 6. The word 'קרחה' is longer than needed, so it can teach both the ברייתא's laws and the women's exemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the verse only meant to teach the ברייתא's laws, the shorter 'קרח' would have been enough. The extra form shows the תורה meant to give us more. So the גזירה שוה is not 'used up,' and איסי's source for exempting women stands.

steps.whatToRemember: The extra form 'קרחה' (instead of 'קרח') lets one word teach two things: the ברייתא's laws about bald spots, and the גזירה שוה that exempts women.

steps.title: רבא's reason for איסי: learning from תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רבא says איסי exempts women because he links ״בין עיניכם״ in the bald-spot פסוק to ״בין עיניכם״ in the פסוק about תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is איסי's reason. He learns ״בין עיניכם״ from תפילין. Just as women are exempt from תפילין, so too women are exempt from the ban on making a bald spot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a new explanation for why איסי says women are not included in the bald-spot ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bald-spot פסוק says not to make baldness ״בין עיניכם״, and the תפילין פסוק uses the same words. רבא links the two. Women are exempt from תפילין, so they are also exempt here. This is a different route from אביי's reason in the earlier steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who holds that women are not included in the bald-spot ban

תפילין, which women are exempt from

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women are exempt from the bald-spot ban because ״בין עיניכם״ is learned from תפילין, which women are exempt from.

steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי already gave a working source for איסי. If רבא offers a different one, he must have a reason for not accepting אביי's.

steps.title: תפילין themselves are learned from baldness
steps.stepSummary: אביי holds that the link goes the other way: the place of תפילין is learned from the bald-spot פסוק, so the link cannot also teach that women are exempt from the bald-spot ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי would tell you: תפילין themselves are learned from here. Just as there, ״בין עיניכם״ means a place where a bald spot can be made, on the top of the head, so too here, the place where תפילין are put on is the top of the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that אביי already uses the link between the two פסוקים for a different lesson: where on the head תפילין go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bald spot can only be made where there is hair, which is on the top of the head, not literally between the eyes. From this, אביי learns that ״בין עיניכם״ for תפילין also means the top of the head. Since the link is used to teach about תפילין, it cannot be used in the other direction to teach about women and baldness.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Themselves', the תפילין law itself
Learns, derives
The place where תפילין are put on
The top of the head

steps.confusionAlert: ״בין עיניכם״ does not mean literally between the eyes. It means the top of the head above that spot, where hair grows. That is exactly what this step teaches.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that the head-תפילין are put on the top of the head, where hair grows, and not on the forehead between the eyes.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
Tefillin themselves are learned from here:
just as there, it is a place where a bald spot is made,
on the top of the head,
so too here, the place of putting them on
is on the top of the head.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: תְּפִילִּין גּוּפַיְיהוּ מֵהָכָא גָּמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: The link between the two פסוקים is already used for a different lesson

steps.terutzMaskana: For אביי, the link only teaches that תפילין go on the top of the head, so it cannot teach about women
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For אביי, the link between the two ״בין עיניכם״ פסוקים runs the other way: it teaches that תפילין go on the top of the head, where a bald spot can be made. So it cannot also be used to exempt women from the bald-spot ban.

steps.title: What do both learn from 'You are sons'?
steps.stepSummary: Neither אביי nor רבא uses ״בנים אתם״ to exclude women. So what do they learn from those words?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to both אביי and רבא, what do they learn from the words ״בנים אתם״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what ״בנים אתם״ teaches, since neither אביי nor רבא uses it to exclude women. The answer follows next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason given for איסי read ״בנים״ as 'sons, not daughters'. אביי and רבא each found a different source instead. So the words ״בנים אתם״ need a new purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You are sons (children)', the start of דברים 14:1
'What do they learn from it?'

phrases.english: And both according to Abaye and according to Rava,
this "You are sons," what do they learn from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵין לְאַבָּיֵי וּבֵין לְרָבָא, הַאי ״בָּנִים אַתֶּם״, מַאי דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since both rejected the ״בנים״ reason, asks what those words are for
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of ״בנים אתם״ according to אביי and רבא

steps.title: רבי יהודה: sons only when acting like sons
steps.stepSummary: The words are needed for a ברייתא. רבי יהודה says Jews are called God's children only when they act like children.
steps.simpleTranslation: These words are needed for what was taught in a ברייתא: ״בנים אתם לה׳ אלהיכם״. When you act like children, you are called children. When you do not act like children, you are not called children. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ״בנים אתם״ teaches a lesson about being God's children, as explained in a ברייתא by רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads ״בנים אתם״ as conditional. Israel holds the title 'God's children' only while it behaves the way children of God should.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא'
Behaving like children (of God)
Called
The תנא who holds the title is conditional

phrases.english: This is needed for that which was taught:
"You are sons to the Lord your God":
when you act in the manner of sons,
you are called sons;
when you do not act in the manner of sons,
you are not called sons.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by quoting a ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״בנים אתם״ teaches when Israel is called God's children: for רבי יהודה, only when they act like it.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: always called sons
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says Israel is called God's children no matter how they behave, and brings four פסוקים as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: Either way, you are called children. As it says: ״בנים סכלים המה״ (they are foolish children). And it says: ״בנים לא אמן בם״ (children without faithfulness). And it says: ״זרע מרעים בנים משחיתים״ (a seed of evildoers, children who act corruptly). And it says: ״והיה במקום אשר יאמר להם לא עמי אתם יאמר להם בני אל חי״ (where it was said 'You are not My people,' it will be said 'children of the living God').
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי מאיר, who disagrees with רבי יהודה and proves that Jews are always called God's children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first three פסוקים call Israel 'children' even while describing them as foolish, unfaithful, and corrupt. So the title stays even when they sin. The last פסוק shows that even after they are told 'You are not My people,' they will again be called children of the living God.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who holds Israel is always called God's children
Either way, in any case
'And it says', bringing another פסוק as further proof

steps.whatToRemember: The words ״בנים אתם״ are not needed to exclude women for אביי and רבא. Instead they teach about Israel's bond with God: רבי יהודה says it depends on behavior, and רבי מאיר says Israel is always called God's children.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.english: Either way, you are called sons,
as it is stated: "They are foolish sons";
and it says: "Sons in whom there is no faithfulness";
and it says: "A seed of evildoers, sons who act corruptly";
and it says: "And it shall be, in the place where it was said to them,
'You are not My people,'
it shall be said to them, 'Children of the living God.'"

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ אַתֶּם קְרוּיִם בָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי יהודה's view within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Israel is always called God's children, whether or not they act like it.

steps.title: Why does רבי מאיר need so many verses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר keeps adding more פסוקים with the word ״ואומר״ when the first one already seems to prove his point.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of saying 'and it says' again and again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר brought four פסוקים instead of one. This question sets up the next few steps, which explain each extra verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every extra ״ואומר״ suggests that the earlier verse was not enough. The גמרא wants to know what gap each new verse fills.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it says': a word used to bring an extra פסוק as more proof
What? / Why?

phrases.english: What is the reason for 'and it says'?
phrases.notes: He means: why does רבי מאיר keep adding more verses in step 19?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the proof in step 19 needs so many verses
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each extra פסוק adds that the earlier ones did not already prove

steps.title: Even without faith, they are still called children
steps.stepSummary: The first verse only shows that foolish Jews are called children. The second verse shows that even faithless Jews are still called children.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that only foolish people are called children, and that once they lose their faith they are no longer called children. So the second verse says: 'children in whom there is no faith.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the second verse is needed. Without it, we might think being foolish is fine but being faithless ends the relationship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being foolish (״בנים סכלים״) is a weaker failing than having no faith. The verse ״בנים לא אמן בם״ shows that even the worse failing does not take away the name 'children.'

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: brings up a possible objection
Foolish ones
Faith / faithfulness
Come and hear: introduces a proof

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: סְכָלֵי הוּא דְּמִקְּרוּ בְּנֵי,
phrases.english: And if you would say: it is foolish ones who are called children,
phrases.notes: This is the first verse רבי מאיר brought, ירמיהו 4:22, 'they are foolish children.'

phrases.english: but when they have no faithfulness in them
they are not called children –
come and hear, and it says:
'Children in whom there is no faithfulness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 20 by explaining the second verse
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second verse shows that even faithless Jews are still called children, not only foolish ones

steps.title: Even idol worshippers are still called children
steps.stepSummary: You might think faithless Jews are called children but idol worshippers are not. So the third verse calls even corrupt sinners 'children.'
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that people lacking faith are called children, but once they worship idols they are not. So the third verse says: 'a seed of evildoers, children who act corruptly.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the third verse is needed. It raises the level of sin one step higher, to idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Worshipping idols is worse than lacking faith. The verse ״בנים משחיתים״ uses the word for corruption, which hints at idol worship, and still calls them 'children.'

keyTerms.meaning: They worship / serve
Idol worship
Acting corruptly

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: כִּי לֵית בְּהוּ הֵימָנוּתָא
phrases.english: And if you would say: when they have no faithfulness
that is when they are called children,
but when they worship idols
they are not called children –
come and hear, and it says:
'A seed of evildoers, children who act corruptly.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: כִּי לֵית בְּהוּ הֵימָנוּתָא הוּא דְּמִיקְּרוּ בָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer and explains the third verse
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The third verse shows that even idol worshippers are called children

steps.title: After sinning they become full children again
steps.stepSummary: You might think sinners are only called 'corrupt children' and never real children again. So the last verse says they will be called 'children of the living God.'
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think they are called only 'corrupt children' and are no longer called proper children. So the last verse says: 'In the place where it was said to them, you are not My people, it will be said to them, children of the living God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the fourth and final verse is needed. It shows that Israel goes back to being full, proper children of God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third verse still calls them children, but with a bad label, 'corrupt.' The fourth verse shows the full title comes back: 'children of the living God.' This completes רבי מאיר's proof that the bond is never broken.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine, proper children
Not My people
Children of the living God

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, no level of sin, not foolishness, not lack of faith, not even idol worship, takes away Israel's title as God's children. Each verse closes a possible gap.

phrases.english: And if you would say: it is 'corrupt children' that they are called,

come and hear, and it says:

You are not My people,
it will be said to them: children of the living God.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer by explaining the fourth verse
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fourth verse shows that Israel gets back the full title of 'children of the living God'

steps.title: New משנה: Temple service actions done by men, not women
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists eight Temple service actions that apply to men and not to women. A סוטה and a נזירה are the exception: they wave their own מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Leaning hands on an offering, waving, bringing the מנחה to the altar, taking a handful from it, burning on the altar, pinching a bird's neck, catching the blood, and sprinkling the blood: these apply to men and not to women. The exception is the מנחה of a סוטה and of a נזירה, which the women wave themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists Temple actions that only men do, with one exception for women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the chapter's theme of which מצוות apply to women. Here the topic is Temple service. The exception is a סוטה and a נזירה, who wave their own מנחה offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Leaning one's hands on the head of an offering
Waving an offering
Taking a handful from a מנחה
Pinching a bird offering's neck
A woman suspected by her husband of being unfaithful

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the exception as saying a סוטה or a נזירה does all these actions. The exception covers only waving (תנופה) their own מנחה.

and waving, and bringing near,

phrases.notes: The extra letters in square brackets belong to the corrected wording, so read it as וְהַהַקְטָרוֹת.

apply to men and not to women,

which they themselves wave.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The eight listed Temple actions apply to men only, except that a סוטה and a נזירה wave their own מנחה

steps.title: Source that only men do סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins with סמיכה. The פסוק says 'speak to the sons of Israel... and he shall lean,' so men lean their hands and women do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Leaning hands: as it is written, 'Speak to the sons of Israel... and he shall lean.' The sons of Israel lean, and the daughters of Israel do not lean.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through the משנה's list one item at a time. The first item is סמיכה, and the גמרא gives its source in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״בני ישראל״ are read narrowly as 'sons,' meaning men. Since the command to lean hands is addressed to them, women are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Sons of Israel, read here as men only
And he shall lean his hand
Daughters of Israel

phrases.english: GEMARA: Leaning hands.
As it is written: 'Speak to the sons of Israel... and he shall lean' –
the sons of Israel lean,
but the daughters of Israel do not lean.

steps.raayaObject: That סמיכה applies only to men
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 1:2–4, 'Speak to the sons of Israel... and he shall lean'

steps.title: Waving is done by men, not women
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about waving is addressed to 'the sons of Israel,' so men wave and women do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Waving: 'Speak to the sons of Israel... and he shall wave.' The sons of Israel wave, but the daughters of Israel do not wave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second item on the משנה's list, תנופה (waving), and brings a פסוק as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works exactly like סמיכה in the last step. The פסוק opens with 'speak to the sons of Israel' and then commands waving. Because it says 'sons,' the גמרא learns that the rule is for men and not for women.

keyTerms.meaning: Wavings: moving parts of a קרבן back and forth as part of the service
They wave
Daughters of Israel, meaning Jewish women

steps.confusionAlert: Remember from step 24 that the משנה made an exception for waving: a סוטה and a נזירה do wave their own מנחה. This step gives the general rule; those two cases stand out as special exceptions.

phrases.english: Wavings.

steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 7:29–30: 'Speak to the sons of Israel... and he shall wave'

steps.title: Bringing the מנחה near is done by men, not women
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'the sons of Aaron shall bring it near,' so male כהנים do this and not daughters of כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bringing near: as it is written, 'And this is the law of the מנחה... the sons of Aaron shall bring it near.' The sons of Aaron, and not the daughters of Aaron.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק for the third item on the list, הגשה (bringing the מנחה near).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the פסוק says 'sons of Aaron' instead of 'sons of Israel,' because this job belongs to כהנים. The reading is the same: 'sons' means men, so daughters of כהנים do not do it.

As it is written
Bring near (offer)

steps.title: Taking a handful is done by men, not women
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the מנחה is brought 'to the sons of Aaron, and he shall take a handful,' so only male כהנים do קמיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Taking a handful: as it is written, 'And he shall bring it to the sons of Aaron, and he shall take a handful.' The sons of Aaron, and not the daughters of Aaron.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק for the fourth item, קמיצה (taking a handful from the מנחה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person bringing the מנחה hands it to 'the sons of Aaron,' and then the handful is taken. Since the פסוק names the sons, the גמרא learns that daughters of כהנים do not take the handful.

steps.title: Burning on the altar is done by men, not women
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'the sons of Aaron shall burn it,' so only male כהנים do הקטרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Burning: as it is written, 'And the sons of Aaron shall burn it.' The sons of Aaron, and not the daughters of Aaron.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק for the fifth item, הקטרה (burning parts of the קרבן on the מזבח).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the פסוק names 'the sons of Aaron' as the ones who burn. So the burning is a job for male כהנים and not for their daughters.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnings: burning parts of a קרבן on the מזבח
And they shall burn

steps.whatToRemember: For each Temple action on the list, the גמרא finds a פסוק that says 'sons of Israel' or 'sons of Aaron' and reads it as 'sons, not daughters.' 'Sons of Israel' is used for jobs of the owner (סמיכה, תנופה); 'sons of Aaron' is used for jobs of the כהן (הגשה, קמיצה, הקטרה).

phrases.english: Burnings, as it is written:

The sons of Aaron, and not the daughters of Aaron.

steps.title: Pinching is linked to burning, so only male כהנים pinch
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק places מליקה next to הקטרה. Since only male כהנים do הקטרה, only male כהנים do מליקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Pinching: as it is written, 'And he shall pinch... and he shall burn.' Pinching is compared to burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that women do not do מליקה. It does this by linking מליקה to הקטרה, which it already showed is only for men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about מליקה does not mention 'sons of Aaron' on its own. Instead, it puts 'pinch' and 'burn' in the same verse, and the גמרא treats them as one package. Step 29 already showed that הקטרה is only for male כהנים, so מליקה follows the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Pinching: killing a bird offering by the neck

As it is written

steps.title: Starting the proof that only male כהנים receive the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק 'the sons of Aaron shall bring near' for קבלה, and begins to quote an explanation of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Receiving: as it is written, 'And the sons of Aaron shall bring near,' and the Master said:

steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'והקריבו' does not plainly say 'receive.' So the גמרא needs 'the Master's' explanation to show that this פסוק is about קבלה. Once that is shown, 'sons of Aaron' will mean male כהנים only.
